title: mlflow-artifacts tracking URI validation: redact credentials from any error that echoes the tracking URI
answers: Tracing exporter logs a WARNING with my database password when the server runs with --serve-artifacts. How do I stop credentials leaking into logs?
Where does MLflow reject a tracking URI whose scheme is not http or https for mlflow-artifacts artifact URIs?
I'm adding another validation error in the artifact repo that mentions the tracking URI. What must I strip from it before raising?
Why does the 'tracking URI must be a valid http or https URI' error not show the query string or password anymore?
body:
Path: Resolving an `mlflow-artifacts` artifact URI into a concrete repo (trace export, artifact upload/download through the tracking server) passes through `mlflow/store/artifact/mlflow_artifacts_repo.py:_validate_uri_scheme`, which rejects any tracking URI whose scheme is not http/https.
Rule: When an error message includes the offending tracking URI, build it from a redacted form: drop userinfo (everything up to the last `@` in netloc) and also drop params, query and fragment, keeping only scheme, host, port and path. Credentials can sit in the query (e.g. `?password=` or `odbc_connect=...PWD=...`), so userinfo-only stripping is not enough.
Symptom: The tracking server, whose global tracking URI is its own backend store URI, logged a database password in cleartext at WARNING level through the tracing exporter, and that text reached the log aggregator.
Constraints: Applies to messages that echo a tracking or store URI. URIs without credentials keep their scheme, host, port and path, so the message stays actionable. Does not cover other logging paths that print raw URIs.
applies: Error messages raised in the mlflow-artifacts artifact repo that echo a tracking or backend store URI.
says: The server warning logs expose our database password when artifact serving is turned on.
Stop displaying database credentials and connection secrets in tracking server log messages.
Connection errors when uploading artifacts leak sensitive database passwords into shared monitoring tools.
Redact passwords and private connection parameters from artifact storage error messages.
search: Validation errors echoing tracking URIs in mlflow/store/artifact/mlflow_artifacts_repo.py:_validate_uri_scheme must redact credentials by removing userinfo, params, query, and fragments. Keeping only scheme, host, port, and path prevents sensitive database passwords and connection strings from leaking into tracing exporter logs at WARNING level when running with --serve-artifacts. This rule applies to error messages in the mlflow-artifacts artifact repo that echo tracking or backend store URIs, but does not cover other logging paths.
